archetypes.name: contract-parity
archetypes.rationale: The diff adds ~40 CLI entrypoints with exact KV/exit contracts inherited from bash scripts; the static correctness reviewer may miss domain-specific parity requirements around fail-open behaviors, usage-exit preservation, and raw-stdout-vs-emit_kv routing.
archetypes.prompt_body: This diff adds new *_cli.py CLI entrypoint modules (ci_cli.py, git_cli.py, gh_cli.py, merge_cli.py) registering ~40 verbs in cli.py, each inheriting the exact KV-output and exit-code contract of its original bash counterpart. Verify: (1) ci-status always emits exactly four KVs (CI_STATUS, BEHIND_COUNT, FAILED_RUN_ID, CONFLICTED) even when pr_view fails or git-log probes fail, and whether poll_ci's pr_view_ok=False path suppresses a spurious 'pass' status before PR state is confirmed; (2) usage-exit preservation — merge-pr, ci-rerun-failed, ci-decide exit 1 on bad argv while ci-wait and behind-count exit 1/2 respectively on bad argv, not 0; (3) whether raw-stdout-only verbs (resolve-repo, gh remote-repo, gh workflow-path) correctly use print() rather than emit_kv, and whether gh run-logs correctly returns unredacted text; (4) in git_cli.py commit_main, whether passing both --pathspec-from-file and positional file args causes double-staging (git add via add_pathspec_file, then commit_with_trailer also receives pathspec_from_file); (5) whether ci-wait's atomic .done sentinel is written correctly when poll_ci raises an exception with output_file set, and whether the pre-initialized default status/decision values match the shell trap contract. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: migration-lint-regex
archetypes.rationale: The migration_lint.py regex is a deletion-safety gate — false negatives (missing live invocations) risk breaking LARCH_SHIP_PR_IMPL=bash while false positives block valid script retirement, making regex precision security-critical.
archetypes.prompt_body: Focus on python/migration_lint.py's new _ship_pr_live_ref, _script_dir_refs, and _line_references_retired functions, which gate whether scripts can be safely deleted. Verify: (1) whether _ship_pr_live_ref's script_dir_path regex pattern correctly matches $SCRIPT_DIR/basename and ${SCRIPT_DIR}/basename forms while not over-matching unrelated paths containing those substrings; (2) whether stripping comment lines (stripped.startswith('#')) is sufficient to exclude prose mentions — for example, does the check handle lines where a comment follows live code on the same line; (3) whether _script_dir_refs is correctly restricted to same-directory callers (Path(rel).parent == Path(retired_path).parent) and whether this guards against cross-directory false positives where a script in scripts/ uses $SCRIPT_DIR to reference a script in skills/; (4) whether there are live invocation forms that escape all three patterns in _ship_pr_live_ref — for example, invocations using variable expansion like SCRIPT="$SCRIPT_DIR/basename.sh"; $SCRIPT or forms with extra whitespace between source and the path; (5) whether the regex character class [^"'\s;|&)] in script_dir_path could fail to anchor at legitimate invocation terminators like newline or end-of-string. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
